newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes firmer as tone improves.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes firmer as tone improves.

text.p: Gold prices could move higher after a sharp jump in New York late the previous night was maintained in Far East trading early on Friday, dealers said.
Technically gold looked more robust having spent most of the year to date struggling behind other precious metals' rallies.
But some dealers thought gold might move lower before it made another play for fresh recent highs.

"The market is confused about what it does next," one dealer said. "I would not be surprised to see it top the high (of last night at $351.35) but I would not be bullish for it at over $355.00," he added.
Gold fixed at $350.75, its highest fixing since January 29, compared with $345.00 on Thursday afternoon.
The rally sparked in New York late Thursday after a week of improving sentiment as the hedge funds steadily covered short positions.
Helping to fire the rally was a comment from South African Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals that gold sales by the Belgian and Dutch central banks were unlikely to be followed by others.
"How would he know? He said that to re-assure the South Africans and it was exactly what the market wanted to hear," one analyst said.

Meanwhile gold's technical background was improving. "Gold has enjoyed a substantial rally and there is a good likelihood that we have seen the lows for now," said technical analyst Elli Gifford at Investment Research of Cambridge.
However both gold and platinum remained in their downtrends for now, she added.

"I can see them trying to take it higher. It has broken some chart points and it could try $355-$360 but we are talking about a rally in a bear market," said market analyst Ted Arnold at Merrill Lynch.
Gold had created a "triple top" on the April Comex future chart between $348.80 and $349.00 which also suggest some upside potential, one dealer said.
Meanwhile silver had been bought on its dip early on Thursday to be marked up to $5.23/$5.35, a gain of four cents.
Depending on how supportive gold became, silver at $5.40-$5.50 could be viable, dealers said.
Platinum and palladium were both firmer although neither market moved on fresh factors, dealers said.
Platinum was up $3.50 at $369.00/$370.00 and palladium up $2.50 at $134.00/$135.00.
